name: Portugal
headline: Portugal's SNS 24 shows patients who opened their record and asks consent before clinicians look; a May 2026 credential theft tested both.

access.summary: Portugal scored 88.1 on the EU 2025 record-access indicator against an EU average of 82.7, and SNS 24 shows prescriptions, lab results, vaccines and five years of care history. Lei 12/2005 gives a right to the whole record, but the portal is not the full chart.
detail: Lei 12/2005 says health information belongs to the person and the holder may see the whole clinical record, except in justified exceptional cases where it would harm them. Since 2016 a doctor intermediates only if the person asks.
The health regulator ERS says consulting the record is free, while copies (photocopies, CDs) and medical reports may carry a fee. The ERS page gives no response deadline.

Anyone with a health user number can log in to the SNS 24 personal area (gov.pt). The OECD profile lists vaccination records, e-prescriptions, sick leave, living wills, appointments and lab orders and results.

In 2024, 40% of Portuguese adults accessed their record online, against 28% in the EU, but 62% of the most educated did so versus 19% of the least educated (OECD). Since early 2026 the app also shows five years of care history (E-Konomista).

control.summary: Clinicians cannot open the national record without the patient's authorisation, set in SNS 24 or given at the visit, and patients can see every access. Lei 58/2019 requires that people be notified of any access to their health data.
detail: Article 29(6) of Lei 58/2019 says the data subject must be notified of any access to their health data, and the controller must provide that tracing and notification mechanism.

The ACSS manual for the RSE professional area says access is checked against the patient's SNS 24 authorisations, with separate permissions for SNS and for private or social sector providers. Without one, the patient must authenticate. Unauthorised simplified access shows vaccines only.
Pplware (May 2026) says the personal area shows several years of who viewed the data and lets people grant or refuse access to history, exams, medicines, consultations and nursing visits.

The system was tested in May 2026, when one doctor's stolen credentials were used against many records. Parents learned of it from SNS 24 access notifications (HealthNews), which shows the log works, though authorisation did not stop the misuse.

privacy.summary: Health data has strong statutory protection, but in May 2026 a doctor's stolen credentials were used to improperly access data of more than 100,000 SNS users. The regulator CNPD opened an inquiry and reported possible crimes to prosecutors.
detail: Lei 58/2019 applies the GDPR in Portugal. Article 29 limits health data access to need to know, binds everyone handling it to secrecy, and calls for differentiated permissions, prior authentication and electronic logs of access.
Lei 12/2005 requires health units to prevent improper third-party access to clinical records and systems, including backups, and to separate health and genetic data from other personal data.

In May 2026 the CNPD received hundreds of complaints about improper access using a doctor's credentials at ULS Alto Minho, affecting more than 100,000 people including children (ECO). The ULS said the records reached were administrative, not clinical (HealthNews).

In 2018 the CNPD fined the Barreiro Montijo hospital centre 400,000 euros for giving clinical-record credentials to staff who should not have them (Jornal de Negócios). The OECD notes several high-profile ransomware attacks on the health system.

commercial.summary: Lei 12/2005 says health information may be used only for care, health research and other uses set by law, and bans insurers from using genetic data. A 2021 law stops lenders and insurers using past cancer and other overcome conditions.
detail: Article 3 of Lei 12/2005 makes health units custodians, not owners, of health information, which cannot be used for purposes other than care, health research and others set by law. Article 4 requires written authorisation for other uses by the health system.
Article 12 bars insurers from requesting or using genetic information, including family history, to refuse cover or raise premiums.
Lei 75/2021 creates a right to be forgotten: after set periods, lenders and linked insurers may not collect or use health information about a serious condition the person has overcome or mitigated.
We found no Portugal-specific rule on consumer health apps or data brokers beyond the GDPR, so those fall under general data protection law.

journey.summary: A central agency, SPMS, gives every public provider and most private ones a common data centre, network and software, and the RSE timeline lists episodes from all SNS institutions. Private providers have no legal duty to share records.
detail: The OECD describes a highly centralised architecture run by SPMS, supplying every public provider and most private ones with a common data centre, secure network and standard software.

There is no legal requirement for private providers to make patient data electronically available to others, which leaves gaps in the shared record (OECD). Some primary care units still run legacy software and hospitals are moving to a new platform in phases.
The RSE professional timeline lists prescriptions, results, discharge notes, consultations, emergencies, admissions, surgeries and SNS 24 contacts across SNS institutions (ACSS manual).
Lei 95/2019 says health information circulation must rely on interoperability and interconnection of SNS systems. For EU exchange, SPMS is scaling MyHealth@EU services (OECD).

clinical.summary: With the patient's authorisation, a doctor or nurse sees a timeline of episodes from every SNS institution and can open each source record over the health network. Data held only by private providers is often missing.
detail: The RSE professional area shows a chronological list and a map of all the patient's contacts with SNS institutions, with a link to each institution's local electronic record (ACSS manual).
Opening the local record needs a VPN connection to the health information network. Without it the professional sees only the history without detail.

Access needs the patient's prior authorisation in SNS 24 or authentication at the visit. Lei 12/2005 limits record access to the treating doctor and supervised staff, as strictly needed. Private-sector data is not legally required to be shared (OECD).

research.summary: Anonymised health data may be used for research without individual consent under Lei 12/2005, and no general opt-out exists yet. Trials need informed consent and ethics approval, and Portugal was first to list a dataset on HealthData@EU.
detail: Article 4(4) of Lei 12/2005 lets anonymised health information be provided for research. Lei 58/2019 article 31 requires minimisation and anonymisation or pseudonymisation where possible, and allows consent covering several research areas.
Lei 21/2014, the clinical research law, requires informed consent, a prior interview with the investigator, a right to withdraw without effect on care, and insurance.
In November 2025 Portugal became the first member state to publish a dataset on the HealthData@EU central platform (AFP, reprinting SPMS). The OECD says the HealthData@PT access body is being set up.
The EHDS opt-out from secondary use applies from March 2029 (European Commission). Until then we found no national opt-out.

ai.summary: Portugal relies on EU law for clinical AI, with no national AI law. ANACOM supervises the AI Act and the health regulator ERS protects fundamental rights for high-risk AI, both EU-required roles.
detail: The government chose ANACOM in September 2025 as main market supervisor and contact point for the AI Act (ECO).
ERS was notified to the European Commission as an authority protecting fundamental rights under Article 77(2) of the AI Act for high-risk systems in Annex III, and commits to guide the sector (ERS).
SPMS is piloting AI for clinical triage, antimicrobial alerts and dermatology (OECD). We found no binding national clinical-AI guidance.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 moved high-risk duties to 2 December 2027 for standalone systems and 2 August 2028 for AI in medical devices (Cuatrecasas).
